question: Does God know and value me?
truth: You are a beloved child of God with eternal worth.
title: God Knows and Loves You
speaker: Alan T. Phillips
summary: Your worth does not depend on success, appearance, or the approval of others. Heavenly Father knows you personally, Jesus Christ offers redemption and relief, and your identity as a child of God gives lasting purpose to your life.
application: It is easy to measure our worth by grades, success, appearance, relationships, or what other people think of us. This message teaches that every person is a child of God, which means our deepest worth comes from Him rather than from achievements or approval. Because God's love does not rise or fall with our successes and failures, our value does not disappear when life goes wrong. Understanding this gives us a more lasting foundation for knowing who we are and why our lives matter.

question: Why am I here?
truth: Your life has divine purpose, even when you cannot yet see the whole plan.
title: Your Divine Nature and Eternal Destiny
speaker: Dale G. Renlund
summary: You came to earth with divine identity and eternal potential. Remembering who you are helps you make choices based on God's plan rather than temporary pressure, comparison, or fear.
application: The world often encourages us to define ourselves by success, popularity, comparison, or what other people expect from us. This message teaches that every person has divine worth and a purpose that reaches beyond temporary achievements. Knowing that our lives are part of God's larger plan helps us see that today's pressures do not determine our ultimate value or potential. That perspective can give greater meaning and direction to the choices we make.

question: Why is Jesus Christ central to everything?
truth: Jesus Christ is not merely part of the answer—He is the answer.
title: The Answer Is Always Jesus Christ
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
summary: Jesus Christ is the center of Heavenly Father's plan. Through His teachings, Atonement, Resurrection, and covenant power, we receive forgiveness, healing, direction, peace, and the hope of eternal life.
application: Life offers many places to look for happiness, direction, healing, or answers when something feels missing. This message teaches that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and the Savior, who came to help every person return to God and receive forgiveness, healing, peace, and hope. Through His teachings, His sacrifice for us, and His victory over death, He made possible things we could not accomplish for ourselves. Understanding who He is helps explain why Christians place Him at the center of their faith and their lives.

question: Can Jesus Christ really help with my burdens?
truth: Jesus Christ is not an added burden; He is the source of relief.
title: Jesus Christ Is Not Our Burden; He Is Our Relief
speaker: David J. Wunderli
summary: Following Jesus Christ does not mean carrying every burden alone. The Savior offers strength, rest, and relief as we come to Him and allow His grace to support us through difficult seasons.
application: Life can sometimes feel heavy with stress, worry, or challenges that seem too much to carry alone. Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Savior of the world, willingly experienced the pain, sorrow, and struggles of every person so He could understand us perfectly. Because of that, He does not simply tell us to be strong—He walks beside us, strengthens us, and helps us carry what feels too heavy to bear on our own. Even when life does not change overnight, we can move forward with hope because we never face it alone.

question: Can I change after making mistakes?
truth: Because of Jesus Christ, your past does not have to determine your future.
title: Jesus Christ and Your New Beginning
speaker: Patrick Kearon
summary: The Savior offers more than one chance to begin again. Through repentance and His Atonement, setbacks, weakness, and sin can become turning points instead of permanent definitions of who you are.
application: Everyone makes mistakes, and it is easy to believe those mistakes define who we are or determine what our future can become. This message teaches that Jesus Christ came to make change possible through His Atonement, offering forgiveness, healing, and a new beginning to anyone who turns to Him. He does not erase our experiences, but He can transform them into opportunities for growth and hope. Understanding this reminds us that our past does not have to define our future because, through Jesus Christ, change is always possible.

question: Do I have to be perfect before God can help me?
truth: Worthiness is faithful direction, not flawless performance.
title: Worthiness Is Not Flawlessness
speaker: Bradley R. Wilcox
summary: God does not expect immediate perfection. Through the grace of Jesus Christ, we can repent, improve, and continue growing while still receiving divine help along the way.
application: Many people feel they have to be perfect before they are worthy of love, forgiveness, or a fresh start. This message teaches that every person has weaknesses and makes mistakes, while Jesus Christ is the only one who lived a perfect life. Because He was perfect, He could do something no one else could—take upon Himself our sins so we could be forgiven, healed, and become better. God does not expect us to become perfect all at once; through Jesus Christ, we can keep learning, changing, and growing one step at a time.

question: How can I find peace when life is still difficult?
truth: Peace comes through Jesus Christ, not through perfect circumstances.
title: Finding Personal Peace
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
summary: The Savior's peace can enter our hearts before our circumstances improve. As we receive His peace, we become better able to calm fear, strengthen others, and carry hope into troubled situations.
application: Difficult circumstances can leave us feeling anxious, discouraged, or overwhelmed. This message teaches that Jesus Christ offers a different kind of peace—not the absence of problems, but strength and hope while we are still facing them. Because He understands our fears and struggles, He invites us to come to know Him by talking with God through prayer, learning His teachings, and trying to apply them in everyday life. As our understanding of Him grows, we can find greater calm and confidence even before our circumstances improve.

question: What should I do when anxiety or conflict surrounds me?
truth: Prayer may not remove every storm immediately, but it brings divine support within it.
title: Prayers for Peace
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
summary: Turning sincerely and repeatedly to Heavenly Father brings peace and abiding support. Prayer helps us place our fear before God, recognize His presence, and move forward with greater spiritual steadiness.
application: When life feels uncertain, many people wonder where they can turn for peace and direction. This message teaches that prayer is more than simply asking God for help—it is a personal conversation with our Heavenly Father, who knows us, loves us, and listens to every sincere prayer. Through prayer, we can share our fears, questions, gratitude, and hopes while seeking His guidance and comfort. As we continue building that relationship with Him, we become more aware of His peace, strength, and direction, even when life's challenges remain.

question: How does God guide me personally?
truth: God guides us through the Holy Ghost as we seek, recognize, and act.
title: Promptings of the Spirit
speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
summary: Personal revelation becomes clearer as we invite the Holy Ghost, recognize spiritual impressions, and act faithfully on what we receive. Guidance often grows through small moments of obedience.
application: Life is full of important decisions, and it can be difficult to know which path to take. This message teaches that God guides His children through the Holy Ghost, who helps us recognize truth, brings peace to our minds and hearts, and gently encourages us toward what is good. These quiet thoughts and feelings are often called promptings. As we learn to recognize them and compare them with God's teachings, we become more confident in making decisions that lead us toward what is good and true.

question: How can I avoid confusing my own wishes with revelation?
truth: Revelation works within God's truth, commandments, and appointed order.
title: A Framework for Personal Revelation
speaker: Dale G. Renlund
summary: The Holy Ghost gives real personal guidance, but revelation does not contradict God's commandments or assign authority that belongs to someone else. Humility, scripture, prayer, and obedience help protect us from deception.
application: When making important decisions, it can be difficult to know whether a thought or feeling comes from God or from our own desires. This message teaches that God guides us through the Holy Ghost, but His guidance will always agree with His truth and teachings rather than lead us away from them. As we learn about God's word through scripture, prayer, and the teachings of His prophets, we become better prepared to recognize His guidance with greater confidence. Understanding this helps us make decisions based on lasting truth instead of temporary emotions or personal preferences.

question: How can I remain faithful during overwhelming trials?
truth: Faith in Jesus Christ creates spiritual steadiness before the storm is over.
title: Steady in the Storms
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
summary: Life's storms test our spiritual foundation. We remain steady by becoming humble, relying on Jesus Christ, remembering God's promises, and continuing faithful practices when circumstances feel uncertain.
application: Life's greatest challenges can leave us wondering whether there is a way forward. This message teaches that faith means believing Jesus Christ knows us, loves us, and will help us even when we cannot yet see how everything will work out. As we learn about Him, talk with God through prayer, and apply Christ's teachings in our daily lives, our confidence in Him can grow stronger. Faith does not always remove life's storms, but it can give us courage and strength to keep moving forward because we know we are not facing them alone.

question: What can I hold onto when I feel discouraged?
truth: Hope in Christ sees beyond the pain of the present moment.
title: The Triumph of Hope
speaker: Neil L. Andersen
summary: Hope in Jesus Christ is more than wishing for easier circumstances. It is confidence that His promises are real, His Resurrection is certain, and His peace can sustain us while answers are still unfolding.
application: Loss, disappointment, or uncertainty can make it feel like things will never get better. This message teaches that hope is more than simply wishing for better days—it is confidence in what Jesus Christ has made possible. After He died, He rose to life again, showing that death is not the end of our journey. Because of Him, God promises that life continues after death and that families can be reunited again through His plan. Understanding this gives us hope that even our greatest losses are not forever.

question: How should followers of Christ treat other people?
truth: True discipleship is revealed most clearly in how we treat one another.
title: Peacemakers Needed
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
summary: Followers of Jesus Christ reject contention, cruelty, and personal attacks. Peacemaking requires courage, self-control, charity, and the willingness to respond in the Savior's way—especially when emotions are strong.
application: Conflict is a natural part of life, but the way we respond to it can strengthen or damage our relationships. This message teaches that Jesus Christ showed a different way to treat people—with patience, kindness, forgiveness, and love, even when others were unkind to Him. He asks His followers to become peacemakers, meaning people who choose words and actions that heal rather than create more hurt. Living this way can bring greater peace into our families, friendships, workplaces, communities, and our own hearts.

question: How can one ordinary person make a meaningful difference?
truth: The Savior can multiply a willing offering, even when it feels small.
title: Here Am I, Send Me
speaker: Susan H. Porter
summary: Like the child who offered loaves and fishes, we do not need wealth, influence, or extraordinary ability to serve. Jesus Christ can magnify sincere efforts and use them to bless more people than we can see.
application: It is easy to believe that making a difference requires special talents, great influence, or perfect circumstances. This message teaches that Jesus Christ often works through ordinary people who are willing to serve. Just as He multiplied a small offering of food to bless thousands of people, He can magnify sincere efforts and use them to bless more people than we could accomplish on our own. Understanding this reminds us that even small acts of kindness, love, and service can have a meaningful and lasting impact.

question: What should guide the choices I make today?
truth: An eternal perspective gives greater meaning to daily decisions.
title: Think Celestial!
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
summary: Daily decisions shape eternal direction. When we remember Jesus Christ, covenant promises, and our ultimate destination, temporary pressure loses some of its power and faithful choices become clearer.
application: Every day, we make choices that shape the direction of our lives, even when they seem small. This message teaches that Jesus Christ invites us to look beyond temporary success, pressure, or immediate rewards and consider what has lasting, eternal value. Seeing life from God's perspective helps us recognize that today's decisions influence the people we become tomorrow and the relationship we build with Him. Understanding this can help us choose what brings lasting joy, purpose, and peace rather than only what feels good in the moment.
